rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and glad Halcyon Threshold came up at the meetup. I'm not in a position to go on record by name right now — I need to clear public statements with my employer first, and I'd rather not get ahead of that. Happy to revisit once that's sorted, or point you toward others in the space if that's useful for your deadline. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Declined the reporter's quote request (Larkin Dispatch)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Hi, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. I'm not able to sign on as a public signatory right now — I have an employer clearance process on outside/public statements that I need to finish first. I may be able to join future letters once that's resolved. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: declined the Corvid Institute open-letter sign-on

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Thanks, this is really helpful. I'd like to apply, but I have an internal disclosure/approval step of my own to clear first, on roughly the same timeline. I'll aim to get you a proposal before the 30th if that clears in time; if not, I'll ask about the next round. Appreciate you holding a spot in mind. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: told Emberfall's Idris you're interested but have your own internal approval step to clear first

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — genuinely glad to hear this. Halcyon Threshold is still taking shape, but here's something concrete that would help a lot: a short landscape scan of where small, independent contributions (not big labs) seem most neglected right now. Specifically, something like: what Alignment Commons, Compute Commons, Emberfall Fund, and similar groups are and aren't funding or covering, and where a solo operator with evenings/weekends, some Python, and a few thousand dollars could plausibly do something checkable and useful — leaning toward evaluation/measurement work rather than research or advocacy. Even a one-page summary with sources would be a big help in deciding what to actually do next. No rush — whenever you have an hour or two. Thanks again, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman (offered to help) with a concrete, non-public task: a landscape scan of where independent AI-safety work is neglected.
